title: Marijuana Vs. Alcohol: Which Is Worse For You?
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant compare marijuana and alcohol on overdose risk, drug interactions, long-term health, pregnancy, crime, and driving impairment. They open with tour dates, cover legalization history (Obama's 2014 New Yorker interview, states that legalized recreational pot), and close with a listener mail question about overlap with other podcasts. Key points: alcohol causes about 88,000 deaths a year per CDC, about half from binge drinking, while a fatal THC overdose is considered practically impossible; alcohol interacts dangerously with prescription drugs; a 2015 Danish study linked chronic pot use to lower sperm count; pregnancy guidance advises no alcohol; marijuana users show lower intimate partner violence than drinkers in one 2014 study; stoned drivers tend to drive slower while drunk drivers drive more aggressively; blood THC thresholds (five nanograms per milliliter, with Sweden pushing one) are controversial.

segments.title: Tour dates and opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts announce upcoming live tour dates in Boston, Washington D.C., St. Louis, Cleveland, and Englewood, Colorado, then begin with banter about Obama's 2014 New Yorker interview on pot.

segments.title: Legalization history and the pot vs. alcohol comparison
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the spread of recreational marijuana legalization since Washington and Colorado in 2014, the Clinton inhale controversy, and why the pot-versus-alcohol debate is now an academic question.

segments.title: Overdose risk: alcohol vs. marijuana
segments.summary: The CDC estimates about 88,000 alcohol-related deaths per year, about half from binge drinking, with alcohol poisoning a real risk. Overdosing on THC is considered practically impossible, with an estimated 150 joints needed.

segments.title: THC potency, edibles and the blood-brain barrier
segments.summary: The hosts explain THC content per gram, losses from burning, and why edibles are metabolized by the liver into a more potent form. They note edible-related emergency room visits and the danger to children.

segments.title: Drug and alcohol interactions and prescription medicine
segments.summary: Alcohol can speed or block liver enzymes that metabolize medications, causing over- or under-dosing. Marijuana can impair coordination, and both impair judgment.

segments.title: Long-term health: liver, sperm count, lungs
segments.summary: Alcohol damages the liver and can lead to cancer, though some heavy drinkers are spared, possibly due to genetics. A 2015 Danish study found a 28 percent drop in sperm count among men smoking more than one joint a week. Marijuana smoke's lung effects are less clear.

segments.title: Pregnancy and alcohol vs. marijuana
segments.summary: The CDC estimates 3.3 million US women risk exposing a baby to alcohol; fetal alcohol spectrum disorders can result from drinking in early pregnancy. Studies show no clearly safe level of alcohol, while marijuana data are less clear.
topics: pregnancy alcohol fetal alcohol spectrum disorder

segments.title: Crime, partner violence and TV crime shows
segments.summary: A 2014 study found marijuana users had lower intimate partner violence rates than drinkers or non-users. A survey of jailed offenders found 37 percent were drinking when they committed their crime. The hosts then discuss Cops and Forensic Files.

segments.title: Driving high vs. driving drunk
segments.summary: Drunk drivers tend to be aggressive and impulsive, while stoned drivers tend to overestimate impairment and drive slower. Some states have reduced traffic deaths after legalization. Blood THC thresholds of 5 ng/mL (US states) and 1 ng/mL (Sweden) are debated, and roadside field sobriety tests are weaker for marijuana.
topics: driving under the influence of marijuana

segments.title: Personal anecdote about a field sobriety test and closing thoughts
segments.summary: Chuck recounts being pulled over in college and given a field sobriety test while sober. The hosts note that the legal and research landscape is still developing and will be revisited in ten years.

segments.title: Listener mail: podcast topic overlap
segments.summary: Listener Neil asks whether the show coordinates topics with other podcasts. The hosts say they do not check with each other, and overlap happens occasionally.
